(a) Extension of Computer Technology and Equipment Donation.—
        (1) In general.—Section 170(e)(6)(G) is amended by striking “2005” and inserting “2007”. 
        (2) Effective date.—The amendment made by paragraph (1) shall apply to contributions made in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2005.  
    (b) Expansion of Charitable Contribution Allowed for Scientific Property Used for Research and for Computer Technology and Equipment Used for Educational Purposes.—
        (1) Scientific property used for research.—
            (A) In general.—Clause (ii) of section 170(e)(4)(B) (defining qualified research contributions) is amended by inserting “or assembled” after “constructed”. 
            (B) Conforming amendment.—Clause (iii) of section 170(e)(4)(B) is amended by inserting “or assembly” after “construction”.  
        (2) Computer technology and equipment for educational purposes.—
            (A) In general.—Clause (ii) of section 170(e)(6)(B) is amended by inserting “or assembled” after “constructed” and “or assembling” after “construction”. 
            (B) Conforming amendment.—Subparagraph (D) of section 170(e)(6) is amended by inserting “or assembled” after “constructed” and “or assembly” after “construction”.  
        (3) Effective date.—The amendments made by this subsection shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2005.

fable.w: This section only amends tax code provisions on charitable contribution deductions for computer technology and scientific property, extending a date and adding the words "or assembled", and sets effective dates. The tempting reading is that "contributions" or "donation" suggests outside-party involvement, but these are private charitable donations for tax purposes, not consultation, comment, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or a right to sue over a federal decision. No outside party is brought into any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only changes a date and adds wording to tax-deduction definitions for donations of computer equipment and scientific property. Words like "contribution" and "donation" refer to private charitable gifts. They do not bring anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision. Nothing here requires or allows consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or lawsuits.
opus.s: Section 170(e)(6)(G) is amended by striking “2005” and inserting “2007”.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Internal Revenue Code regarding charitable contributions for computer technology and scientific property. It changes dates and definitions but does not establish any mechanism for public comment, advisory committees, consultation with outside entities, or other forms of participation as defined. The actors involved are Congress (amending the law) and the IRS (enforcing it), with no required interaction with outside parties in the decision-making process described in this text.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section amends tax code provisions related to charitable contributions, it involves non-profits or donors (outside parties) interacting with the government. However, the text itself only describes technical amendments to statutory definitions and effective dates. It does not establish a process for consultation, comment, or participation by outside parties in the decision-making process. The interaction described is purely legislative amendment of tax rules, not a procedural requirement for public input.
